top3.headline: On Anthropic's IPO day, Perplexity's CEO calls Opus 5.5 the best model
top3.whyItMatters: Even competitors name Anthropic's model the leader, which shapes vendor choices for your teams.

top3.headline: Perplexity keeps Decider free for 3 weeks, claims near 20% share
top3.whyItMatters: Teams can test decision models at no cost while vendors compete hard on price.

top3.headline: Theo reports strong Gemini 4 Neon results on long engineering tasks
top3.whyItMatters: Long-horizon coding is where agents save the most time, so leadership there matters.

items.title: Masad: build your own Muse-like personal agent with one prompt
items.takeaway: Amjad Masad posted 'Build your own Muse-like personal agent with one prompt', with a link to the details.
items.soWhat: Personal agents like Muse are becoming something a small team can build, not only buy.

items.title: Replit's Amjad Masad expects others to copy its agent contracts
items.takeaway: Masad says having a contract with your agent is a paradigm he expects many to copy from Replit. Details are in his linked post.
items.soWhat: Setting terms with an agent before it starts work is turning into a product feature.

items.title: Theo reports strong Gemini 4 Neon results on long engineering tasks
items.takeaway: Theo says he is seeing 'insane results from Gemini 4 Neon on long horizon eng work' and will share more soon.
items.soWhat: Long-running coding work is where model choice matters most, so watch for his evidence.

items.title: DeepMind's Koray Kavukcuoglu: no single test will show AGI arrived
items.takeaway: Google DeepMind's SVP says progress will look like models becoming less spiky and more reliable, not a single benchmark moment.
items.soWhat: Judge AI by how reliably it does your work, not by benchmark headlines.

items.title: LangSmith AI Search turns plain-words questions into filters
items.takeaway: Queries such as 'frustrated users with LLM errors this week' become structured filters, plus an AI check for what a filter cannot express.
items.soWhat: Teams running agents in production can find failures without learning query syntax.

items.title: Benaich: robots now share one model across customer sites
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich says frontier robotic systems like Sereact no longer need a custom model per site; experience at one site improves the model for the rest.
items.soWhat: Shared learning across sites is what lets robotics scale more like software.

items.title: On Anthropic's IPO day, Perplexity's CEO calls Opus 5.5 the best model
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas congratulated Anthropic on its 'historic IPO today' and said Opus 5.5 'remains the best model in the industry by a good margin'.
items.soWhat: Praise from a competitor's CEO on listing day supports Anthropic's model-lead story with new investors.

items.title: Perplexity keeps Decider models free on OpenRouter for three more weeks
items.takeaway: Decider-v1.3 and Flash stay free for another 3 weeks. Srinivas says Perplexity's share of requests on Decision models is close to 20%.
items.soWhat: Free windows are how model makers buy share, so cheap tests are available now.

items.title: Perplexity adds prompt-injection checks to its Context API
items.takeaway: After feedback from Tobi, Perplexity shipped decision models that screen fetched content for prompt injection and score it on custom criteria.
items.soWhat: Web content is a main route for attacking agents, so filtering it before use is basic hygiene.

items.title: Dario Amodei shares his remarks on Anthropic's IPO
items.takeaway: Anthropic posted CEO Dario Amodei's remarks on its IPO. He opens with why he and his co-founders started the company.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab's CEO now speaks to public shareholders, so mission claims meet market scrutiny.

items.title: Perplexity Computer now writes its own agent skills from past sessions
items.takeaway: Brain, which keeps a wiki about your work, now writes and updates agent skills; an improvement agent reads full session trajectories.
items.soWhat: Agents that learn from their own sessions cut the manual work of maintaining skills.

items.title: PrimeIntellect appears compromised; OpenRouter alerted affected users
items.takeaway: Theo says PrimeIntellect appears compromised in a 'very strange way'. No public word from PrimeIntellect yet; OpenRouter told affected users, him included.
items.soWhat: Each model provider behind your agents is part of your security surface, so track who you depend on.

items.title: Meng To: Claude Code built four 3D game characters on its own
items.takeaway: For a three.js game Fable 5.2 built in 2 days, he gave Claude Code a picture of each character plus the Hi3D MCP.
items.soWhat: Agents with the right tool connectors can now produce design assets, not just code.

items.title: Perplexity says Multiagent usage doubled in a single day
items.takeaway: Users pick it for work that splits into parallel pieces: decks, multi-source research, financial analysis, contact lists. Perplexity also shipped Monitor, Orchestrator and Context APIs.
items.soWhat: Parallel agent work is finding real demand in everyday knowledge tasks, not just coding.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro turns five concept images into a 3D house site
items.takeaway: From five concept images it built the Blender model, materials and light, then a scroll-driven site cut open floor by floor.
items.soWhat: Concept-to-client walkthrough is collapsing from weeks of studio work into one agent session.

items.title: Genie 4 lets users reshape a generated world while exploring it
items.takeaway: Users can type prompts mid-exploration to add characters or change the scene, with audio adapting live; available to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers.
items.soWhat: Interactive world models point to new formats for training, simulation and product demos.

items.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, Nasdaq trading next
items.takeaway: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share; the SEC declared its registration effective on November 18 and Nasdaq trading is expected November 19.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab now answers to public markets, so its pace and risk choices get priced daily.

image.alt: @AnthropicAI on X: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, Nasdaq trading next

items.title: Tavi Costa sees silver miners in a capitulation phase
items.takeaway: Record outflows from the sector's biggest ETF, down more than 50% in six months; he says doubting your thesis is normal now.
items.soWhat: A reminder that conviction is tested hardest when flows run the other way.

items.title: OpenAI: AI use by its own researchers keeps rising exponentially
items.takeaway: OpenAI shares new data: researchers' AI use keeps rising exponentially, agents complete longer tasks, humans stay central, and researchers spend more time on safety.
items.soWhat: How a frontier lab uses agents today previews how expert teams will work next.
